newsitem.title: CHINA: Storms hit HK, force cancellation of parade.
newsitem.headline: Storms hit HK, force cancellation of parade.

text.p: Thunderstorms on Wednesday lashed Hong Kong, flooding some areas and forcing cancellation of a carnival parade to celebrate the former British colony's reunion with China.
Eight people were injured in a landslip as the floods disrupted traffic and kept people off the streets on the final day of a five-day holiday to mark Hong Kong's handover at midnight last Monday.
Floats representing animals and Chinese themes stood soggily on a central waterfront promenade as the organisers cancelled the parade.
Rescue teams searched for a woman trapped in her home under a landslip after the torrential rain.
Train services were severely disrupted on the Kowloon Canton Railway because of landslips on the track and hundreds of passengers were forced to take shuttle buses.
Sub-tropical Hong Kong's rainy season starts around late June and runs through September, and many handover-related activities have been rained on during the past few days.
